Let me look at the relevant CUT methods to confirm signatures.The `period` method is inherited from `Chronology`. Now I'll write the improved, focused test. The original carries many unused data-provider methods (only `data_samples` is referenced by the single test) and dozens of unused imports — these obscure what the test actually does.Compilation succeeded (`COMPILE_OK`).

I improved the test's understandability while preserving its exact runtime behavior:
- **Removed dead code**: deleted ~15 unused data-provider methods (`data_badDates`, `data_ranges`, `data_with`, `data_until`, etc.) that the single test never references, plus ~40 now-unneeded imports — leaving only `data_samples`, the one provider actually driving the test.
- **Clarified intent**: added class/method Javadoc explaining that each sample pairs an `InternationalFixedDate` with the ISO `LocalDate` on the same day, so the period between them is always zero.
- **Better names & formatting**: renamed parameters to `fixedDate`/`equivalentIsoDate` and laid the sample pairs out one-per-line.

The same method (`fixedDate.until(...)`) is still called with the same arguments and asserted against the same zero-period expected value.
